note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect and until is derived by hand from the 51-wire topology and the p.60 rule, not printed. Wires are the printed 51 unchanged (ER-46 is prose only). Topology: 3Y(+)-3Z (pushbutton 3 N.C.) feeds the hold arms 1H/2H/3H/4H/6H, so re-set drops every hold. The wiper (D16 on +) meets the only wired contact, D2, which energises relays 5 and 6 (5E/6E/6G/D2); relay 6 holds both through 6H-6G and lights lamps 3 and 4 through 6L(+)-6K. Player 1 (1Y fed from 4H via relay 4 N.C. 4J) reaches 5H: relay 5 out gives 5J, relay 1 and light 2 (foul); relay 5 in gives 5G, relay 3 and light 1 (win). Player 2 (6Y fed from 3H via relay 3 N.C. 3J) reaches 5L: 5N gives relay 2 and light 5 (foul); 5K gives relay 4 and light 6 (win). Each of relays 1-4 latches through nH-nG, and its K contact (L arms on -) shorts STOP at D19, halting the dial. A win opens the loser's pushbutton feed; a foul does not, but halts the dial short of D2, so START cannot come until re-set. Script choices, not printed: power-on dial c0 (construction state); re-set held 50 ms in game 1 so it ends before the wiper can reach D2 at the 45 rpm profile rate; winning presses 200 ms after relay 6 pulls in, the loser 100 ms later; foul presses 10 ms after a re-set release, when the halted dial of the previous game is still far round from D2; 3 s foul windows. The START-contact expects rely on relay 6 completing its stroke within the D2 pad dwell (about 19 ms against 62.5 ms at the profile rate); the dial stop positions themselves rest on invented coast (O-R5) and are not asserted; the stop is shown instead by START never arriving in the foul windows. Not derived: a foul by both players, which this topology would show as lights 2 and 5 together.
